en.title: GPT-6.2: Release Date, Pricing and Budget Planning
en.titleCore: GPT-6.2: Release Date, Pricing and Budget Planning
en.description: What is known about GPT-6.2, its release date and pricing? A sourced guide to the rumors, confirmed models and cost planning.
en.body:
As of November 8, 2026, OpenAI has not announced GPT-6.2 or published its price, release date or specifications in its public model documentation. Names circulating online are not proof of a release. Teams planning budgets should use published prices for available models and treat GPT-6.2 estimates as scenarios.

What is known about GPT-6.2?

Reports describe screenshots of Google Cloud quota filters containing the names gpt-6.2-sol and gpt-6.2-astra. These are reported sightings, not an OpenAI release announcement or evidence that a model is accessible. OpenAI’s model catalog and API changelog are the places to check for a public release. We found no official GPT-6.2 model card or published price when checking on November 8.

A configuration label can exist before a product becomes generally available, and a screenshot alone does not establish what is running behind a request. The name, rollout schedule, capabilities and commercial terms may change.

Is there a GPT-6.2 release date or price?

OpenAI has not published either as of our check. Dates and rates circulating online are predictions, not budget inputs. In its GPT-6.1 Sol announcement, OpenAI lists standard API prices of $2 per million input tokens, $0.10 per million cached input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. Those are GPT-6.1 Sol prices, not GPT-6.2 prices. Provider, service tier and workload conditions can change the amount billed.

What should finance teams put in the forecast?

Keep the current contracted model and rate in the approved forecast. Put any future-model price in a separate sensitivity case, with the assumed adoption date and request volume visible. A lower token price alone does not guarantee a lower bill: longer responses, retries and increased usage can offset it.

How should teams prepare?

  1. Keep a baseline. Record the current model, input and output tokens, latency, task success rate and total cost per successful task.
  2. Use scenarios, not invented prices. For example, at GPT-6.1 Sol standard rates, one million uncached input tokens plus 200,000 output tokens costs $4 before other charges. A hypothetical 25% higher token price would make the same mix $5; this is an illustration, not a GPT-6.2 forecast.
  3. Test on your own workload. If a new model becomes available, compare the same tasks, prompts and success criteria, including retries and tool costs.
  4. Keep rollback possible. Record the model identifier and route with each request, set spend limits and retain a known working configuration.

What about claims that GPT-6.2 is already being used?

Some users claim that requests are being routed to GPT-6.2 Sol. Neither a convincing demo nor an answer to a knowledge question proves which model generated it. Our guide to checking the routing claim explains what different kinds of evidence can and cannot show.

Sources and update policy

We checked the OpenAI model catalog, changelog and GPT-6.1 announcement on November 8, 2026. The reported quota screenshots are described by ArgoLink; we have not independently verified the screenshots. We will need a new official source before treating any GPT-6.2 specification as confirmed.

faq.question: Has GPT-6.2 launched?
faq.answer: OpenAI had not announced GPT-6.2 in its public model documentation when checked on November 8, 2026.

faq.question: How much does GPT-6.2 cost?
faq.answer: OpenAI has not published GPT-6.2 pricing as of that check. GPT-6.1 Sol prices should not be presented as GPT-6.2 prices.
